reason: Registry duplicate-id detection lives at the loader layer. The TypeScript validate() is handed an id-keyed project in which duplicates have already collapsed, so the case is addressed to python only (see its expected.json); the Python reference sees the raw array and reports it.

Once two nodes share an id the dialogue graph is ill-defined. Python merges both copies' outgoing edges under the one id, so node_close stays reachable; TypeScript keys nodes by id and the surviving copy has no edges, so node_close is unreachable. The REACH warning is an artefact of the DUP error both sides report, and it disappears with the duplicate.

The Python reference validates rules.json against the published JSON Schema (whose dice pattern rejects '2x6') before running the RULES check, so one defect is reported twice. TypeScript parses rules.json with a permissive loader and reports the same defect once, from the RULES rule alone.
